scope: Sealed Linux package and execution adapter for the isolated PostgreSQL harness: design, integration contract, implementation, two audit rounds, independent tests and a reproducible release candidate. Local only; nothing ran on Linux, systemd or PostgreSQL, and no host action occurred.

ownerDecisions.diskCap: tmpfs charged to the 512 MiB unit memory limit (mechanism A); watchdog plus IO limit (mechanism B) only as a recorded exception; otherwise refuse
ownerDecisions.osUser: same OS user as the Paper services, with protection layers
ownerDecisions.goPerJob: one owner GO for each of J1 to J4

rootDecisions: The harness runner executeBound owns the job lifecycle; the driver supplies the adapter, monitors, receipt and sanitizer (contract D1).
Time budget: runner wall 285 s, cleanup 30 s, unit RuntimeMaxSec 330, TimeoutStopSec 15 (RD-1).
The cluster superuser is locked out after setup and the lockout is proven by SQLSTATE 28000 (RD-2).
Host tools must be immutable; a Node binary owned or writable by the job user goes to the owner as a decision (RD-3).
Cgroup guard ReadOnlyPaths and ReadWritePaths under mechanism A (RD-4).
J1 is the first Linux proof of the Node permission model (RD-5).
process.kill from the suite child is refused except signal 0 to itself (D49).
Mechanism B is refused by the controller until a B-readiness wave (audit A1-04, A1-08).
Sandbox InaccessiblePaths are required under mechanism A and attested by the driver at run time.

releaseCandidate.reproducible: two builds in separate processes byte-equal
releaseCandidate.verify: strict extract and verify passed on Windows with mode and owner checks skipped

independentTesterRerun.harnessSelftests: 10 suites, 0 failures (accounting 16, service 2, close 8, producer 40, h15 26, stateful 39, suite 22, runner 47, bound 40, bound-callback 9)

checks.safetyMutations: 21 of 21 killed by the independent tester; coder mutation sets left only equivalent survivors
crossChecks: one host contract test passes against the driver fake host and the real Linux binding
the driver process loads 9 adapter and harness files and no product or case module
the capability evaluator and the run binding agree on 53 of 53 host-binding fixtures

audits.A1: ACCEPT_WITH_FIXES: no false-PASS path; one HIGH (SQLSTATE lost in the binding, every real job would fail at the superuser lockout) and seven MED, all fixed except the two mechanism-B items
audits.A1r: READY_FOR_CAP_AND_J1_AFTER_CAP: no new HIGH or MED; J1 only under mechanism A and only after the capability gate passes

deferred: A1-04 and A1-08: mechanism B watchdog and residue (B refused until fixed)
A1-14: residual R3b, the suite child can reach the user bus over AF_UNIX (owner awareness)
low: host-layer immutable rule is stricter than the driver for symlink inputs (fail closed)
openItems.nextCandidate: Candidate 3 with the low fixes and a controller acknowledge command for a lock held after a failure

unprovenUntilJ1: Node permission model, kill guard and Worker preload on Linux
systemd user-unit properties, cgroup delegation and the cgroup guard
tmpfs ownership and sizes inside the unit
real proof, postcheck and receipt timings and the SIGTERM path
nextAction: Owner GO for the read-only capability packet (no host writes; it runs the version commands of node and the PostgreSQL tools and hashes those binaries). Then candidate 3, then the J1 GO if the capability gate passes under mechanism A.

time.method: clock readings and session event times
